# My Simple Bilingual Blog (Eleventy Version)

A basic, multi-file website structure for a bilingual blog, built with Eleventy for easier management of common elements and content creation. Designed for deployment on GitHub Pages.

## Features

*   Static site generated by [Eleventy (11ty)](https://www.11ty.dev/)
*   Uses Nunjucks templating for layouts and logic
*   Content written primarily in Markdown
*   Manages common elements (header, footer, site title) via layouts and global data
*   Basic bilingual structure (EN/BG)
*   Clean URL structure via directory permalinks

## Local Development

1.  **Prerequisites:**
    *   [Node.js and npm](https://nodejs.org/) installed.
    *   Git installed.
2.  **Clone Repository (if needed):**
    `git clone https://github.com/tomsterBG/static-blog.git`
    `cd static-blog`
3.  **Install Dependencies:**
    `npm install`
    *   This reads `package.json` and installs Eleventy.
4.  **Run Development Server:**
    `npm start`
    *   This runs `npx @11ty/eleventy --serve`.
    *   It builds the site into a temporary location and starts a local server (usually `http://localhost:8080`).
    *   The site automatically rebuilds and browser refreshes when you save changes to source files (`src/`).
5.  **Build for Production:**
    `npm run build`
    *   This runs `npx @11ty/eleventy`.
    *   It generates the final static site files into the `_site` directory. This `_site` folder is what gets deployed.

## Project Structure (`src` directory)

*   `_data/`: Global data files (e.g., `site.js` for site title).
*   `_includes/`: Layout files (e.g., `base.njk`, `post.njk`).
*   `assets/`: Static files (CSS, JS, images) copied directly to output.
*   `en/`, `bg/`: Language-specific directories.
    *   `index.njk`: Language homepage template.
    *   `posts/`: Directory for blog posts (Markdown files).
*   `index.html`: Root language selection page.

## Adding Content

1.  **New Post:** Create a `.md` file in `src/en/posts/` or `src/bg/posts/`.
2.  **Front Matter:** Add YAML front matter at the top (see existing posts for examples) specifying `title`, `date`, `language`, `layout: post.njk`, and a `permalink` (e.g., `/en/posts/your-new-post-slug/index.html`).
3.  **Write:** Write content below the front matter using Markdown. HTML is also allowed.
4.  **Link (Optional):** Add the post to the list on the corresponding language's `index.njk` homepage if desired (though eventually, you could make the listing fully automatic).

## Deployment to GitHub Pages (Recommended: GitHub Actions)

1.  **Commit Files:** Commit all your source files (everything **except** `_site` and `node_modules`) to your main Git branch (e.g., `main` or `master`).
2.  **Set up GitHub Actions:**
    *   In your GitHub repository, go to the "Actions" tab.
    *   Choose a "Node.js" workflow template or a specific "Static Site" template.
    *   Configure the workflow file (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`) to:
        *   Check out your code.
        *   Set up Node.js.
        *   Run `npm install`.
        *   Run `npm run build` (which creates the `_site` directory).
        *   Use a deployment action (like `actions/deploy-pages` or `peaceiris/actions-gh-pages`) to push the *contents* of the `_site` directory to your `gh-pages` branch.
    *   Commit the workflow file.
3.  **Configure GitHub Pages:** In Repository Settings -> Pages, set the source to "GitHub Actions".

*Alternatively (Manual Deployment - Not Recommended):*
Run `npm run build` locally, then manually push *only the contents* of the generated `_site` folder to your `gh-pages` branch using `git push -f origin YOUR_LOCAL_BUILD_BRANCH:gh-pages`. This is more error-prone.*
